Subject: FlexiCredit bridge proposal + uplift guardrails for renewal

Hi Jordan —

Thanks again for the call this morning. Per our discussion, I ran a quick model on your current consumption profile and Q3 spikes. As promised, here’s a pragmatic path to keep you under predictable unit costs while we finalize the annual commit:

Proposal (high level)
- 3-month FlexiCredit bridge: Redwood issues billable credits that smooth short-term overages. Credits apply only to hosted API per-token charges.
- Tiered uplift cap: any monthly usage above committed baseline capped at +40% billable uplift (customer pays blended per-token rate tied to tier).
- True-up at renewal: final reconciliation against committed annual volume with option for one-time invoice or credit.

Attachments: I attached a CSV extract of your Q3 usage and a draft term sheet (redwood_flexicredit_term_sheet_v1.pdf).

Ask: Can you confirm whether a 3-month bridge with a 40% uplift cap would be acceptable to your procurement team? If yes, I’ll route to finance for a quick approval and send a DocuSign for signatures.

Thanks —
Karthik

Redwood Inference

Appreciate the fast follow. The 3-month bridge sounds reasonable in principle. A couple of clarifying questions before we engage procurement:

1) How do the credits show up on the bill? We need an auditable line item that our finance team can map to (preferably "FlexiCredit - Redwood").
2) Is the +40% uplift measured against monthly committed baseline or trailing 3-month average?
3) If we exceed the 40% cap in any month, is there an emergency throttle/fallback you can enable (model downgrade) to avoid runaway charges?

Also attaching internal Q3 usage export for your reference (see SaaSWorks_usage_Q3-2026.csv).

Jordan —

Quick answers inline:

1) Billing: Credits will appear as a line item labeled "FlexiCredit Adjustment (Redwood)" with the applied credit amount and description. We can include a ledger id you can reference during PO processing.

2) Measurement window: The uplift cap is measured against your monthly committed baseline (the number you sign for the renewal). For the bridge period we propose measuring uplift against the trailing 3-month average to be conservative and avoid penalizing short spikes.

3) Emergency controls: Yes — Redwood can enable an automatic model downgrade path (to a lower-cost quantized variant) and an opt-in throttle that notifies your on-call before applying hard rate limits. We would default to notification + soft-throttle.

Next step: If that works, I’ll loop in finance and Marissa for final terms and DocuSign. Are you available for a 20-min sync tomorrow at 10am PT?

— Karthik

Jordan —

Thanks for the questions — happy to confirm operational details. A few practical guardrails from our side: 

- Bridge length: 90 days (calendar). We will auto-convert any unused credits to account-level discounts if the full commit executes at renewal.
- Uplift accounting: For the bridge window we will use trailing 3-month average as Karthik suggested; for the renewal true-up we compare to signed annual baseline.
- Rate card: During the bridge you pay an intermediate per-token rate that is between your current on-demand price and the committed rate. The +40% cap refers to billing exposure, not token limit (we still allow burst usage subject to the rate).
- Compliance & audit: We will provide a downloadable usage ledger CSV each billing cycle and a sign-off line on the DocuSign with the ledger id.

Evelyn will confirm final approval on the credit line and any finance conditions (one-time admin fee, ACH terms).

Marissa Cole
Director, Renewals
Redwood Inference

Jordan / Priya —

Finance has reviewed and we can approve a limited FlexiCredit bridge under the following commercial terms: 

1) Credit amount: $150k in FlexiCredits applied over 90 days.
2) Uplift cap: billing exposure capped at +40% month-over-month versus the trailing 3-month baseline during the bridge window.
3) Emergency fallback: automatic model downgrade enabled after 80% of monthly credit consumed; notification and 4-hour cure window before hard throttle.
4) True-up: at renewal we reconcile against the annual committed volume. Any excess usage will be billed at the signed committed rate; any shortfall may convert unused credits to a pro-rated discount at the customer’s election.
5) Admin fee: one-time $5,000 setup fee to cover manual reconciliation and ledger exports (waivable if PO and DocuSign complete in 5 business days).

If you’re good with the commercial outline I’ll ask Ben to issue the DocuSign and the accounting team to prepare the ledger export schedule.

Thanks —
Evelyn Hart
VP, Finance — Redwood Inference
